title: Zoom AI Companion Review (2026): Free Limits, Pro Price
meta_description: Plain-English review of Zoom's AI Companion, now called ZoomMate: what the free plan gives you, what Pro and the $20 ZoomMate add-on cost, and when to skip it.
summary: Zoom's AI Companion, now branded ZoomMate on Zoom's own pages, writes meeting summaries and answers questions about your Zoom calls. The free plan gives you 3 summarized meetings a month. Zoom Pro ($16.99 a user a month, or $14.16 billed yearly) makes summaries unlimited. The full ZoomMate add-on, with agents and workflows, is another $20 a user a month and runs on credits.
one_liner: Zoom's built-in AI that writes your meeting notes and answers questions about calls.
why_care:
If your sales calls, client check-ins, and team meetings already happen on Zoom, this writes the recap so you don't have to. On a paid Pro plan, meeting summaries are unlimited at no extra charge.

If you don't run your meetings on Zoom, skip it.
good_for: Get a written recap of a client call, with next steps, without taking notes yourself.
Join late and ask "What did I miss?" during the meeting (in-meeting questions).
Take AI notes on a Google Meet or Teams call too, using My Notes (3 uses a month free, per Zoom).
Set your own summary format, like "decisions, owners, deadlines" (custom templates, 8 a month on Pro).
Draft a follow-up email or a slide deck from the meeting (ZoomMate add-on; results unverified).
how_to_use:
Step 1: Sign in to Zoom and host a meeting. Free Basic accounts get summaries for 3 hosted meetings a month, per Zoom's pricing page.

Step 2: Turn on the meeting summary from the AI Companion / ZoomMate control in the meeting [CHECK: the button label may have changed with the ZoomMate rename]. Tell everyone on the call that the AI is taking notes.

Step 3: Near the end, ask it this, then compare the answer to what you heard:

What did we agree to, who owns each next step, and by when?
what_youll_get:
A written summary of the meeting and answers to questions about what was said, inside Zoom. Treat it as a first draft: read it before you send it to a client.

We have not run our own tests for this review.
missing: Free Basic is tight: summaries and in-meeting questions for 3 hosted meetings a month, 20 AI queries a month, and 40-minute meetings.
Zoom's pricing page says AI features don't apply to users with Basic permissions on paid accounts. Every person who needs the AI needs a paid license.

The agents, unlimited AI note-taking, deep research, and third-party workflows are in the ZoomMate add-on at $20 a user a month ($16.67 billed yearly), and AI actions use up credits (2,200 a user a month).
Zoom's "Workflow Automation" unlimited runs are a limited-time promo; Zoom says pricing and terms may change after it ends.
If your calls happen on Google Meet or Teams, a dedicated notetaker like Otter.ai fits better.
verdict: If you already pay for Zoom Pro, the unlimited meeting summaries are a free win, so turn them on. The $20-a-user ZoomMate add-on is credit-metered agent stuff most small businesses don't need yet, which keeps this at "It's alright."
price_free: Zoom Workplace Basic, $0: meeting summaries and in-meeting questions for 3 hosted meetings a month, AI note-taking (My Notes) 3 uses a month, 20 AI queries a month, 40-minute meetings, up to 100 participants.
price_paid: Listed in USD per user per month: Pro $16.99 billed monthly or $14.16 billed yearly (unlimited meeting summaries, 30-hour meetings, 10 GB cloud recording). Business $21.99 monthly or $18.33 yearly (300 participants). ZoomMate add-on $20.00 monthly or $16.67 yearly (2,200 AI credits a month, agents, workflows, deep research, live voice translation). Checked Nov 24, 2026.
when_to_use:
* Your meetings already run on Zoom.
* You already pay for Zoom Pro or Business, so summaries cost nothing extra.
* You forget to write down who promised what on calls.
* You want one tool for meetings, chat, and notes instead of adding another app.
when_to_skip:
* Your meetings run on Google Meet or Teams.
* You're on free Zoom and have more than 3 meetings a month worth summarizing. Pay for Pro or use a dedicated notetaker.
* You don't want an AI listening to client calls, or your clients don't.
* You're tempted by the ZoomMate add-on but don't have a real workflow for agents to run.
missing_text:
Here's how the money works, as listed on Zoom's pricing pages.

Plan	Listed price (USD, per user per month)	What you get for AI
Basic	$0	Summaries for 3 hosted meetings a month, 20 AI queries, My Notes 3 uses
Pro	$16.99 monthly / $14.16 yearly	Unlimited meeting summaries and queries, 8 custom summary templates a month
Business	$21.99 monthly / $18.33 yearly	Same AI as Pro, plus 300-person meetings
ZoomMate add-on	$20.00 monthly / $16.67 yearly	2,200 AI credits, unlimited AI notes, agents, workflows, deep research

The catches:

* The ZoomMate add-on runs on credits. Zoom says some features don't use credits, but AI actions and agents do. Watch the meter.
* Zoom's ZoomMate pricing page lists 40-minute, 100-person meetings under the ZoomMate plan, which suggests the add-on alone doesn't include Pro meetings [CHECK].
* "Billed yearly" prices mean paying for the year up front.

Bottom line: If you're on Zoom Pro, use the summaries you already pay for. Hold off on the add-on until you can name the job you'd give it.
privacy:
ZoomMate connects to your meetings, chats, calendar, and apps like Google Drive, Salesforce, and Jira, per Zoom's product page, and it keeps a "memory" of your past interactions. Zoom says its answers are "permission-aware."

We did not read Zoom's AI privacy terms for this review [CHECK: whether Zoom uses your meeting content to train AI, and how long it keeps it]. Let people know when the AI is taking notes, and keep confidential client calls out of it until you've read Zoom's terms.
alternatives:
* Otter.ai: If you want AI meeting notes that work across Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams. Read our Otter.ai review.
* Microsoft Copilot: If your team lives in Teams and Microsoft 365. Read our Microsoft Copilot review.
* Fathom: A free AI notetaker for calls [CHECK: not reviewed here].
